author: Good Enough
description:
Kimball’s Anti‑Rheumatic Ring was a wildly popular piece of jewelry once marketed as a medical breakthrough. Advertised as a ring that could cure rheumatism, neuralgia, headaches, and almost any disease you could name, it became a nationwide fad long before modern science stepped in.

From bold claims to clever marketing, this is one of the strangest medical fads you’ve probably never heard of.
